description:
Spec: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 commit 9344aec ("refactor: implementation-defined emoji authorization").

Spec text: "Authorization for CustomEmoji/set is implementation-defined, for both Space-scoped and server-global emoji. Returns forbidden SetError when unauthorized."

Current state: handle_emoji_set in chat-server/src/emoji.rs delegates to update_object/destroy_object — there is no policy hook for whether the caller is allowed.

## Acceptance

- New ChatBackend method:
  ```rust
  fn may_set_custom_emoji(
      &self,
      _caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
      _account_id: &Id,
      _target_space_id: Option<&Id>,
      _op: EmojiSetOp,
  ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<bool, Self::Error>> + Send {
      async { Ok(true) }
  }
  ```
  where `EmojiSetOp` is a small enum in chat-server::backend module: { Create, Update, Destroy }.
- handle_emoji_set in chat-server/src/emoji.rs consults may_set_custom_emoji BEFORE calling the underlying create_object/update_object/destroy_object. On false: SetError::Forbidden with description "Implementation-defined emoji authorization denied this operation."
- MemoryBackend implements may_set_custom_emoji as: server-global (target_space_id = None) → true; Space-scoped → true if caller's principal_id is in the Space members list, else false. Document this in rustdoc as "demonstration only; not a production policy."
- Test: MemoryBackend with no Space → CustomEmoji/set create with no spaceId → succeeds
- Test: MemoryBackend with Space, caller is a Space member → succeeds
- Test (requires test-only Backend per integration.rs precedent): Backend that always returns false → CustomEmoji/set returns Forbidden SetError

## Out of scope

- Per-permission gating (e.g. "only manage_emoji holders") — that's the deployment's may_set_custom_emoji impl
- Rate-limiting (separate hook if needed)
title: Layer B: ChatBackend::may_set_custom_emoji + CustomEmoji/set handler integration
